pro_course_detail.title: Independent Study in Philosophy
pro_course_detail.description:
Learn English by taking a one-on-one course in Philosophy with a university professor. Let's talk and read about the big questions together: 

What is philosophy, and what does it mean to love wisdom?
What is truth and how can we distinguish truth from falsity in a "post-truth" world? 
What is art and how can we understand its place in a world so dominated by scientific thinking? 
How can we understand our roles as individuals within a larger community?
How can we determine if something is good or evil? 
What or who is God, and why do people believe in his existence, or not? 
What is phenomenology? 

These are just a few of the questions past students have been interested in. Together, we can plan a reading list and set of questions that meet your interests and needs.

pro_course_detail.title: Attacking Faulty Reasoning, Logic, Fallacies
pro_course_detail.description:
This class is a more philosophical approach to critical thinking. Improve your logic and critical thinking through one of two methods:
(1) Learn to slowly and carefully read philosophical texts that discuss these issues. through how to improve critical thinking through particular texts. We will begin with Platonic dialogues. 
(2) Work through a textbook of Informal Logic, which will train you to think more clearly by training you to recognize and eliminate common patterns of errors, or logical fallacies. We will use Damer's "Attacking Faulty Reasoning" (6th or 7th edition).

pro_course_detail.title: Classic Texts:  What is Freedom?
pro_course_detail.description:
What is Freedom? This idea is central to human life, and it is of course a major part of the "American dream." But what does this word mean? Is freedom about external circumstance, or internal state? And how has it so shaped our popular imagination? This course will give you a mini-version of what we call in English a "great-books" course: an introduction to classic texts that have shaped the history and culture of the anglophone world, in America and beyond. 

*READING*: Each session will feature a selection of works from a variety of genres and from across different periods, to improve your range of literary comprehension and to give you new angles to think from - from literature to poetry to political philosophy.*

*WRITING*: Each session will include an assignment of a short response paragraph to the readings to work on your writing skills.

*SPEAKING*: Each session, come with questions or reflections, and we can work out these themes together, as you expand your English and learn to think about big ideas!

[*Too busy to write? Too busy to read? That's ok! The advantage of one-on-one tutoring is that we can adapt to your needs and schedule.]

Let's work on polishing your English skills while reflecting on important themes together!

teacher_info.teaching_style:
My teaching method is as follows:

Step 1: Choose one sound to improve. There are 44 sounds in American English, and the most important to pronounce accurately are: the "R" sound, the "short i", and the "short a".

Step 2: Learn how to create the sound. Know what your tongue and mouth should be doing.

Step 3: Drill the sound with the IPA until it is comfortable.

Step 4: Learn the most common words that use your target sound. 

Step 5: Practice simple sentences using the most common words.

Step 6: Advanced practice (paragraphs, minimal pairs, tongue twisters etc).

Step 7: Test the sound again. Do you still need more practice?

teacher_info.about_teacher:
I believe that after understanding the basics of the language, students learn best by learning a language in context. In other words, after attaining a basic understanding of reading, writing, listening and speaking, it is best for students to continue their learning journey based on topics that interest them.

pro_course_detail.title: Improve Your Vocabulary, Accent and Pronunciation with Texts
pro_course_detail.description:
This format is best for those who want to expand their vocabulary and improve their accent.  Many people do not know that accent is more than just your pronunciation; it also includes your intonation patterns, the rhythm of your speech, and the fluency of your speech.  You can have perfect pronunciation but still not sound like a native if you lacking in the other areas of your speech.  

These classes are made to specifically work on accent reduction and building your vocabulary.  To do this, we will use text a digital text which you will read it aloud.  We will focus on specific vowel and consonant sounds , syllable and word stress, and rhythm patters to help you sound more like a native.  

Since we will be using native level content, you will also be exposed to new vocabulary, phrases and sayings.  We will discuss the text and I will help you with any doubts you have.  The texts will be on topics of interest to you so that you can use the vocabulary in your daily life.  The possibilities are endless and include:
- News articles
- Blog posts
- Short stories
- Passages from novels

You can also bring any material that you like, for example a book you are reading, a text for work, a novel for school, etc.  As long as you have the text in a digital format, we can use it in our sessions.
